subtype: Approach: counts back from a fixed date to set small deadlines [Action]
passage: Kavya's school in a village near Nashik had its science fair on Friday. On Saturday evening she sat on the veranda with the calendar and counted backwards on her fingers. 'Fair is Friday. Poster ready Thursday, so Chetan Sir can see it. Experiment on Tuesday, in case it goes wrong. Materials before that, so I buy them Sunday when Papa goes to the market.' She put the days on separate sticky notes: Sun buy, Tue experiment, Thu poster, and stuck them on her desk. On Tuesday the first try failed, but she still had two days to fix it. On Friday the poster was dry and the experiment worked.

qa.q: On which day did Kavya plan to run the experiment?
qa.a: Kavya planned the 'Experiment on Tuesday', in case it goes wrong.

qa.q: What did Kavya want to leave time for by running the experiment on Tuesday?
qa.a: Kavya wanted time to fix it if it went wrong, which shows she was a little worried about it failing.

qa.q: What other approach could help Kavya keep to her dates?
qa.a: Kavya could ask Papa or Chetan Sir to look at her sticky notes on Wednesday, since a check-in shows early if something is behind.

qa.q: How might Chetan Sir see Kavya's plan?
qa.a: Chetan Sir probably sees a student who manages her time well, since the poster was ready before the fair.

grounding: Shows a girl counting back from Friday to set the dates for the poster, the experiment and buying materials, and marking each on a sticky note.

subtype: Approach: counts back from a fixed date to set small deadlines [Action]
passage:
The science fair at Xin's school in Singapore was on Friday, and her project was whether bean seeds sprout faster in the dark. On Saturday evening she sat at her desk, stuck.
Her friend Nkechi, on a video call, asked, "So when do you start?"
"I'll work it out backwards," Xin said. "Friday I carry it in. So the poster has to be finished by Thursday. The beans need two days to show anything, so they go in the jars on Tuesday. That means I need cotton wool and jars by Sunday."
She wrote each day on its own yellow sticky note and pressed them in a row above her desk: SUN buy, TUE plant, THU poster.
"You're so organised," Nkechi said.
"I just don't want to be gluing the poster at midnight again," Xin laughed.

qa.q: On which day do the beans go in the jars?
qa.a: The beans go in the jars on Tuesday.

qa.q: What was Xin worried about when she planned backwards?
qa.a: She was worried about rushing again, as she didn't want to be gluing the poster at midnight like last time. 😅

qa.q: What else could Xin add to the sticky notes, and why?
qa.a: She could add a spare day before Thursday in case the beans are slow, so a small delay does not ruin the poster.

qa.q: How does Nkechi see Xin's row of sticky notes?
qa.a: Nkechi is impressed and calls Xin organised, seeing the plan as something clear and easy to follow.

grounding: It shows a girl counting back from a Friday science fair to set small dated steps and writing each on a sticky note above her desk.

subtype: Approach: counts back from a fixed date to set small deadlines [Action]
passage:
Study hour at the girls' hostel of Shanti Vidyalaya was silent except for fans. Mehak stared at the notice: Model Exhibition, Friday.
Last year she had stayed up Thursday night and her volcano had cracked on the table. This time she took a pencil and turned her diary to the week.
Friday: carry the water filter model to the hall. Thursday: chart must be done. Tuesday: pour muddy water through and time it. Sunday: get sand, gravel and a bottle from the canteen and the sports store.
She wrote each day on a sticky note and stuck them in a line on the edge of her desk.
Vikas Sir, doing his rounds, stopped and read them. "Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday. Good gaps between them." He tapped Tuesday. "Give yourself Wednesday too, in case the water stays muddy."

qa.q: What did Mehak's volcano do last year?
qa.a: Her volcano cracked on the table after she stayed up Thursday night.

qa.q: How might Mehak have been feeling when she read the Friday notice?
qa.a: She was probably anxious, remembering the cracked volcano, and determined not to repeat the rush.

qa.q: Which change suggested by Vikas Sir would make the plan stronger, and why?
qa.a: Keeping Wednesday free as a spare day helps, because if the filter test fails on Tuesday she can still fix it before Thursday.

qa.q: How might Vikas Sir see Mehak's sticky notes?
qa.a: He sees a careful plan with good gaps and wants to help her protect it from surprises, which is why he suggests a spare day.

grounding: It shows a girl counting back from a Friday exhibition to set small deadlines, writing each day on a sticky note on her desk.
